answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-backed reputation that decays. A new identity starts with no trust and must earn it by completing verifiable work, like an opal that only gains its shine after careful cutting. Reputation is tied to a locked stake, so spinning up fake agents costs real money each time. A yarrow patch spreads slowly, and trust should grow the same way: gradually, through repeated honest service. If one identity misbehaves, its stake is slashed and its history dies with it, so the cost of a sybil spiral keeps rising while honest agents keep their earned standing.
